id: # Coop mod rule additions. Starsector merges a mod's data/campaign/rules.csv onto the vanilla
# ruleset, so only the added/overriding rows live here.
# How the merge works (verified against the 0.98a bytecode, not assumed):
#   - Rules.load calls the merged-CSV loader in LoadingUtils with idColumns=["id"] on
#     "data/campaign/rules.csv".
#   - That loader walks the resource-source list and keeps the FIRST row it sees for a given id;
#     any later source's row with the same id is dropped outright.
#   - StarfarerLauncher registers every enabled mod path into the resource loader (com.fs.util.C)
#     at index ZERO, i.e. ahead of the core data dir. So mod rows come first, and a mod row whose
#     id matches a vanilla row REPLACES it; the vanilla row never reaches the rule engine.
#   - Rules.load skips any row whose id starts with '#', which is what makes these comment rows
#     (and vanilla's own #ngcDisableSpacerOption) inert. Rows whose id columns are all empty are
#     dropped by the loader, so blank ',,,,,,' separator lines are safe.
#   - Duplicate ids WITHIN one file are a hard RuntimeException at load. Vanilla gets away with
#     six rows all keyed '#' because the CSV parser drops a row whose RAW first character is an
#     unquoted '#' before the loader ever sees it. Our comment rows are QUOTED, so their first
#     character is '"' -- they survive the parser and do occupy an id. So keep every comment line
#     below textually unique, and use empty rows (not repeated quoted '#' rows) as spacers.
# (1) COOP TEST START -- a 6th option in the "Your most recent occupation was as..." list.
# Grants a Ziggurat + 1,000,000 credits + crew/supplies/fuel so two clients can get into a
# real fight without grinding an early game first. Chains into NGCDifficultyOptions, exactly
# like the vanilla explorer/merc/freelancer options, so the rest of creation is unchanged.
# MUST be gated or removed before any public release -- see docs/PHASE14_SPIKE_NOTES.md.
coopZigguratStart
script:
SetTooltip coopZiggurat "COOP TEST START - not intended for normal play.

A Ziggurat-class phase battleship (Experimental variant), 1,000,000 credits, and a full complement of crew, supplies and fuel.

Exists so a coop session can start with something worth fighting over."
options: 6:coopZiggurat:COOP TEST - a phase experiment survivor, commanding a Ziggurat (1,000,000 credits)

id: coopZigguratPicked
script:
NGCAddShip ziggurat_Experimental
NGCAddCredits 1000000
NGCAddCargo RESOURCES crew 50
NGCAddCargo RESOURCES supplies 100
NGCAddCargo RESOURCES fuel 150
FireAll NGCDifficultyOptions

id: # (2) FORCED NORMAL DIFFICULTY + FORCED TUTORIAL SKIP, for every start option.
# This one row replaces the vanilla ngcDifficulty row (same id -> vanilla row is dropped, see the
# merge notes at the top). Vanilla ngcDifficulty is the ONLY rule with trigger NGCDifficultyOptions,
# and NGCDifficultyOptions is fired only from rules.csv (ngcExplorerPicked, ngcMercPicked,
# ngcRandomPicked, ngcKitePicked, ngcShepherdPicked and our coopZigguratPicked) -- no engine code
# fires it. Replacing the row therefore removes the question outright instead of racing it.
# Why replace rather than add a second row: FireAll <trigger> runs EVERY matching rule (it collects
# rules.getAllMatching and calls runScript on each, unlike FireBest which applies only the single
# best match). An added row with a fresh id would run ALONGSIDE the vanilla question, not instead
# of it. Sharing the id is what makes this exclusive.
# The script body is the vanilla ngcSkipTutorialPicked body with NGCSetDifficulty normal in front,
# so picking an occupation (and, for the Wolf/Wayfarer starts, a second ship) drops the player
# straight into the campaign. This also bypasses the vanilla NGCCanSkipTutorial gate, which is
# intended -- a fresh profile can still start coop. The spacer start (option 5) never fires
# NGCDifficultyOptions: ngcSpacerPicked already sets normal itself and ngcSpacerContinue already
# runs this same skip body, so it is untouched and already compliant. (It is also hidden unless
# enableSpacerStart is turned on -- settings.json defaults it to false.)
# WHY FORCE NORMAL. Difficulty is stored per client (CharacterCreationData.setDifficulty ->
# SectorAPI.setDifficulty, persisted as <difficulty> in saves/save_*/descriptor.xml) and is read
# through Misc.isEasy(). A host/guest mismatch would give an asymmetric world. What 'easy' changes
# in 0.98a, from settings.json + the Misc.isEasy() call sites:
#   - easyPlayerDamageTakenMult 0.75 / easyPlayerDamageDealtMult 1 (settings.json): player ships
#     take 25% less damage. Combat-engine side, so it would be per-client -- two players in the
#     same fight with different survivability.
#   - easySensorBonus 500 (settings.json; SettingsAPI.setEasySensorBonus): +500 sensor range.
#     Detection is dist <= observer.getMaxSensorRangeToDetect(target), so this changes which NPC
#     fleets each client sees -- i.e. it desyncs the replicated fleet view, not just the HUD.
#   - easySalvageMult 1.5 (settings.json): applied in FleetEncounterContext.gatherLoot (battle
#     salvage), CoreScript debris-field value, and SalvageEntity.generateSalvage (every salvage
#     drop). Loot quantity feeds the shared world state, so this is world-shaping, not cosmetic.
#   - easyOfficerLevelMult 1 (settings.json): FleetFactoryV3 officer levels on generated NPC
#     fleets. A no-op at the vanilla default of 1, but it is host-authoritative world generation.
#   - ha_maxMonthlyProgressEasy 30 vs ha_maxMonthlyProgress (HostileActivityEventIntel
#     .getMaxMonthlyProgress): hostile-activity event pacing. World-shaping.
#   - CampaignTutorialScript guard-fleet composition -- moot here, the tutorial is skipped.
# So a mismatch would produce a host-difficulty-shaped shared world (salvage, NPC fleets, event
# pacing) with per-client combat and sensor modifiers layered on top. Symmetric Normal instead.
# WHY FORCE THE TUTORIAL SKIP. The vanilla tutorial rewrites Galatia system state
# (TutorialMissionIntel, respawn flags, the Ancyra/Jangala contacts), which would diverge host and
# guest in a seed-locked coop campaign. Nothing else fires NGCTutorialOptions once the vanilla
# ngcEasyPicked/ngcNormalPicked rules are unreachable, so the tutorial question is never asked.
# Caveat: if a third mod also defines trigger NGCDifficultyOptions under a different id, FireAll
# would run both it and this row. Coop v1 is not built for third-party content mods.
# Revisit at Phase 23 packaging -- see docs/PHASE14_SPIKE_NOTES.md.
ngcDifficulty
script:
NGCSetDifficulty normal
$ngcSkipTutorial = true
NGCAddCharacterPoints 1
NGCSetStartingLocation Corvus -2500 3000
NGCAddStandardStartingScript
NGCDone

id: # (3) DEV-MODE QUICK STARTS REMOVED. The two vanilla >>(dev) quick start options are gated on
# $global.isDevMode and run their own script bodies straight to NGCDone -- they never fire
# NGCDifficultyOptions, so the forced-normal/skip-tutorial row above cannot reach them. They also
# set NGCSetWithTimePass false and drop the player in hyperspace at -10000/-10000 with a hand-built
# fleet, i.e. a different starting world state per client if only one player picks one. Four rows,
# all replaced by id: the two AddNewGameChoices rows stop the options from being offered at all,
# and the two NewGameOptionSelected rows are neutered as well so a stale $option value cannot
# reach the vanilla script body. $coopDevStartsDisabled is never set anywhere, and a missing
# memory key evaluates false, so all four conditions are permanently unsatisfiable.
initNewGameChoicesDev
initNewGameChoicesDev2
ngcDevStartOption
ngcDevStartOption2
